title: Corrupt-config recovery never offers the existing good backup — and the next save destroys it
existing_state: Every save copies the previous config.json to config.json.bak (Services/ConfigurationService.cs:116-120), so after a corruption event (e.g., a partial write — the save itself is non-atomic WriteAllText) a last-good backup almost always exists on disk. But the corrupt-load path (ConfigurationService.cs:91-102) only copies the corrupt file to config.json.corrupt (JsonFileWriter.TryBackupCorrupt is a copy, Utilities/JsonFileWriter.cs:103-118), sets ConfigLoadError, and returns factory defaults. Form1 surfaces this as a passive, ownerless OK-only warning (Form1.cs:350-354) shown before ApplyTheme runs at Form1.cs:406 — so DialogTheme.ResolveDarkMode(null) finds no themed form and renders a light dialog for dark-mode users (UI/DialogTheme.cs:621-624, 766-781). The dialog never mentions config.json.bak, offers no restore and no 'open folder' action. Critically, the corrupt content still sits in config.json, so the very next Save() (e.g. the silent startup update check writing LastCheckTime) copies the corrupt file over config.json.bak before writing defaults — permanently destroying the only good copy of the entire preset library, environments, and saved state.
recommendation: In ConfigurationService.Load's catch block, attempt to parse config.json.bak before falling back to defaults; if it parses, show a recovery dialog from the constructor: 'Your settings file was corrupted. A good backup from your last session is available (config.json.bak, saved <last-write-time>).' with [Restore backup] (File.Replace .bak over config.json, reload), [Open data folder], and [Continue with defaults]. Rename/copy the corrupt file with a timestamp and guard the .bak from being overwritten while ConfigLoadError is set (skip the .bak copy in Save() until one clean save has happened). Pass the dark-mode flag explicitly (config.DarkMode is already loaded) so the dialog matches the theme. The non-atomic WriteAllText at ConfigurationService.cs:144 is a separate durability fix.
user_benefit: config.json holds everything — presets, environments, host snapshots. Today a single corruption event silently converts a fully recoverable incident into permanent loss of all of it, with the user shown only a vague mis-themed warning while the app destroys the recovery asset seconds after launch. A one-prompt restore turns this into a non-event.

TryBackupCorrupt copies (corrupt stays in place as config.json)
4-arg Show resolves dark mode from open forms; none exist during the ctor, falls back to light

mockup_idea: Dialog mockup: warning icon, 'Your settings file was corrupted. A good backup from your last session is available (config.json.bak, saved 2 min ago).' Buttons: [Restore backup] [Open data folder] [Continue with defaults]. Dark-themed variant shown.

verification.notes: Traced end-to-end and every element holds. The corrupt-load catch (ConfigurationService.cs:91-102) copies the corrupt file to .corrupt but leaves it in place as config.json and never consults .bak — a repo-wide search confirms no code ever reads or restores config.json.bak. Save() (line 118) unconditionally copies config.json over .bak with no ConfigLoadError guard, and the default-on startup update check (CheckOnStartup=true, Form1.cs:14983 Update→Save) fires this seconds after launch, overwriting the last-good backup with corrupt content before writing defaults. Save is non-atomic File.WriteAllText (line 144), making the corruption precondition realistic, and the warning dialog is indeed ownerless/OK-only and renders light-themed because it runs before ApplyTheme with no forms in Application.OpenForms. Critical severity is justified under the data-loss rubric: the app itself automatically destroys the sole recovery copy of presets, environments, and saved state. | impact check: Traced end-to-end and every link holds, including the worst part: backup destruction is automatic, not hypothetical. UpdateSettings.CheckOnStartup defaults to true, and the silent startup check writes LastCheckTime via _configService.Update (Form1.cs:14983) even when the check fails offline — so the first Save after a corrupt load copies the still-corrupt config.json over config.json.bak (overwrite:true) seconds after launch. No code anywhere reads or restores .bak. The trigger is realistic because Save uses non-atomic File.WriteAllText on a constantly-rewritten file, while the repo's own JsonFileWriter.WriteJsonAtomic (atomic + .bak) sits unused by ConfigurationService — making the fix both sound and cheap. Critical is justified: a recoverable incident becomes permanent loss of presets/environments/saved state with zero user action. [updated refs: Utilities/JsonFileWriter.cs:103-124 (TryBackupCorrupt spans through 124); all other cited refs are accurate as of branch 0.51.23]

title: Multi-host run dialog is a cramped fixed 420x580 gate with no filter or bulk-select — and it forgets every option (parallelism resets to 1) on each run
existing_state: FolderExecutionDialog opens for EVERY preset run on more than one host (Form1.cs:12283-12301 via ExecutionDialogPolicy.ShouldPromptForPresetExecutionOptions = hostCount > 1) as well as for folder runs (Form1.cs:12850-12853). The form is hard-fixed at 420x580 with FormBorderStyle.FixedDialog and MaximizeBox=false (FolderExecutionDialog.cs:52-55); both the preset list and the host list live in 375x94 panels (~5 visible rows, FolderExecutionDialog.cs:69-71, 99-101). There is no Select All/None/Invert affordance and no filter box anywhere in the file — for the core persona (200 network devices daily) excluding 10 devices means scrolling and clicking through a 94-pixel-tall box every single run. Worse, the dialog is constructed fresh each time with hardcoded defaults: Parallel hosts = '1' (FolderExecutionDialog.cs:182), Stop on first error unchecked (:149-154), Sequential preset mode checked (:139) — nothing is persisted (AppConfiguration has no FolderExecution fields). The engine batches by ParallelHostCount (SshExecutionService.cs:636-691), so one forgotten keystroke means the 200-host run silently executes one host at a time. The 'Run 1 Presets' caption at :353 also never pluralizes.
recommendation: Rebuild FolderExecutionDialog with a resizable dock-based layout (Sizable + MinimumSize, host list fills remaining space, geometry persisted). Add a filter TextBox above the host list plus All/None/Invert links and the live 'n of m' counter; since FolderExecutionOptions.SelectedHostIndices is index-based against the snapshot (FolderExecutionDialog.cs:343, consumed Form1.cs:12297-12300), filtering must hide rows visually while preserving original indices. Persist last-used options (ParallelHostCount, StopOnFirstError, RunPresetsInParallel, SuppressPresetNames) in AppConfiguration/WindowState — or keyed per preset/folder — and prefill at both construction sites. Optionally add a 'Remember these options / don't ask again' checkbox bypassable with Shift+Run. Fix the 'Run 1 Presets' pluralization while in there.
user_benefit: This is the single most frequently seen dialog for anyone running against a fleet. Resizable + filter + bulk-select + remembered options turns a daily multi-minute scroll-retype-and-click chore into one click, and eliminates the silent accidentally-sequential run when the user forgets to re-enter the parallel count.

verification.notes: Traced end-to-end and every claim holds: the dialog gates every >1-host preset run (Form1.cs:12283 via ExecutionDialogPolicy hostCount>1) and every folder run (12850-12853); it is hard-fixed at 420x580 FixedDialog with 375x94 list panels, no filter, no bulk-select; it is constructed fresh each time with Parallel hosts "1", Sequential checked, StopOnError unchecked, and AppConfiguration persists none of it. title: Host grid has no filtering or sorting — target selection at 200+ hosts is scroll-and-click only
existing_state: Every grid column is forced NotSortable on add (Form1.cs:4304-4308); header click selects the column instead of sorting (Form1.cs:4263-4272). There is no search/filter UI for the host grid — the only filter box in the app belongs to the preset tree (InitializePresetSearchFilter, Form1.cs:8967-9037). Selection aids are limited to Select All / Deselect All / Invert in the grid context menu (Form1.cs:6523-6546). So 'run this preset on all hosts where site=DC2' — the core fleet selection task — requires visually scanning hundreds of rows and clicking checkboxes one by one. The FolderExecutionDialog host list is likewise a flat unfiltered CheckedListBox (FolderExecutionDialog.cs:104-116).
recommendation: Add a filter row above dgv_variables: a text box matching against all columns (or a chosen column), hiding non-matching rows via Row.Visible, plus 'Check all visible' / 'Uncheck all visible' actions. Filtering avoids the unbound-checkbox-column reorder hazard that real column sorting would introduce with the DataTable-bound grid; if sorting is wanted later, snapshot/restore the Select column by Host_IP. Mirror a simple filter box into FolderExecutionDialog's host list.
user_benefit: Selecting a meaningful subset of a 300-host fleet (by site, role, OS column, etc.) becomes a one-line filter plus one click instead of minutes of scrolling, and eliminates wrong-host mistakes.

title: Enter key confirms the destructive action in some delete prompts but cancels in others
existing_state: The app has two themed confirmation primitives with inverted Enter semantics. DialogTheme.Confirm sets AcceptButton = btnNo and styles No as primary (UI/DialogTheme.cs:577-582), so Enter safely declines — used by Clear Grid (Form1.cs:5603) and JobListDialog's delete-job / clear-job-history (JobListDialog.cs:1377, 1261). DialogTheme.Show → ShowCore sets AcceptButton to the FIRST button (Yes) and styles it primary (UI/DialogTheme.cs:724, 729) — used by Delete Folder (Form1.cs:8178, 8224, plus the YesNoCancel variant at 8148), Delete History Entry (Form1.cs:14352), Delete ALL History (Form1.cs:14378), and Delete Environment (EnvironmentDialog.cs:486-494, which also persists to disk immediately). So 'Clear all history for this job?' defaults Enter to No while the visually identical 'Delete all history?' defaults Enter to Yes — a reflexive Enter irreversibly wipes all execution history, a preset folder, or an environment. Additionally, Confirm's message label is fixed at Size(310, 56) with AutoSize=false (UI/DialogTheme.cs:546-556), silently clipping messages longer than ~3 lines, while ShowCore auto-sizes up to 560px (UI/DialogTheme.cs:681-707).
recommendation: Pick one policy — destructive prompts default to the safe answer — and enforce it in one place: extend ShowCore with a defaultButton/dangerous parameter (mapping to AcceptButton + primary styling), set it to No/Cancel at the destructive call sites, and reimplement Confirm as a thin wrapper over ShowCore so there is a single Yes/No code path (which also fixes the message clipping for free). Keep Enter=Yes only for non-destructive questions (e.g., 'Reload file from disk?'). Audit the ~15 destructive Show(YesNo) call sites.
user_benefit: A user who reflexively hits Enter never wipes all history, a folder of presets, or an environment by accident — and the same action always behaves the same way in every window.

evidence.note: Confirm: AcceptButton=No, No styled primary (Enter=No)
ShowCore: AcceptButton=first button=Yes, Yes styled primary (Enter=Yes)
Delete folder / delete entry / delete ALL history confirms ride the Enter=Yes path
Delete environment via Show(YesNo) — Enter deletes, and the delete persists immediately
Same-concept deletions via Confirm — Enter = No
Confirm fixed Size(360,160), label AutoSize=false Size(310,56) — long messages clip

mockup_idea: Side-by-side screenshots of the two Yes/No dialogs ('Clear all history for job X?' vs 'Delete all history?') with the focused/primary button highlighted and an 'Enter presses this' arrow, showing the polarity flip; an 'after' frame showing both defaulting to the safe button with the destructive button secondary.

verification.notes: All cited code and call sites check out, but the headline mechanism is wrong: Confirm's AcceptButton=No is inert. WinForms gives Enter to the focused button, and initial focus lands on Yes (first in tab order; nothing in DialogTheme sets focus) — verified with a .NET 8 probe replicating Confirm exactly (ActiveControl=Yes, Enter clicked Yes). So there is no Enter polarity flip: reflexive Enter presses Yes in ALL these prompts, including the 'safe' Confirm ones, and Confirm's No-styled-primary visual actively misleads (looks like Enter=No, fires Yes) — the hazard is broader than claimed, the inconsistency is visual-only. The recommendation stands but is incomplete: setting AcceptButton/primary styling alone won't fix it; the safe button must also receive initial focus (tab order or ActiveControl), since the focused button always wins Enter. Label-clipping claim confirmed as written.

title: Environment Manager: Cancel button doesn't cancel — every edit and destructive action persists to disk immediately
existing_state: EnvironmentDialog presents classic Save/Cancel semantics (_btnSave/_btnCancel with DialogResult.OK/Cancel, EnvironmentDialog.cs:249-250, AcceptButton/CancelButton at 264-265), but nothing is actually staged. Every list selection change calls PersistCurrentEnvironmentDetails() (EnvironmentDialog.cs:403-414), which writes description, label color, variables, and vault-profile binding straight through EnvironmentService.UpdateEnvironmentDetails to config on disk (802-823) — and silently swallows any write failure (819-822). New/Duplicate/Rename/Delete/Import all execute immediately through the service (427, 449, 471, 499, 595). BtnSave_Click's only real effect is setting SelectedEnvironmentName so Form1 switches environments (639-643). A user who deletes an environment, fat-fingers a variable value, or imports over an existing environment and then clicks Cancel has still permanently committed all of it — the opposite of what the button promises.
recommendation: Pick one model and make the UI honest about it. Option A (preferred): stage edits in an in-memory working set (clone the environment list on open; route New/Duplicate/Rename/Delete/Import and detail edits against the clone) and commit everything in one EnvironmentService transaction on Save — mirroring how SettingsDialog batches its ~80 settings into a single _configService.Update (SettingsDialog.cs:2663). Option B (cheap): keep immediate-apply but remove the false affordance — rename Save to 'Switch & Close' and Cancel to 'Close', and add a small caption ('Changes are saved as you go').
user_benefit: Users can experiment safely in the environment manager and trust Cancel to mean cancel — today a misclick on Delete or a bad import is unrecoverable even after cancelling the dialog.

evidence.note: Save/Cancel buttons with DialogResult semantics implying a staged transaction
Selection change persists details to disk via EnvironmentService; exceptions swallowed
New/Rename/Delete/Import act immediately; Save only sets SelectedEnvironmentName
In-house precedent: SettingsDialog stages everything into one Update on Save

mockup_idea: EnvironmentDialog footer before (Save/Cancel) and after (single Close + 'changes apply immediately' hint, with 'Switch to selected' as the primary action) — or the transactional variant keeping Save/Cancel but with a pending-changes indicator.

verification.notes: Traced end-to-end and accurate: every list selection change and New/Duplicate/Rename/Delete/Import writes straight to config.json (UpdateEnvironmentDetails -> SaveEnvironmentState -> ConfigurationService.Update -> Save), PersistCurrentEnvironmentDetails swallows write failures, and BtnSave_Click only sets SelectedEnvironmentName (Form1 uses DialogResult solely to decide whether to switch environments — no rollback exists). Only nuance: unflushed detail edits on the currently selected environment ARE discarded if Cancel is clicked before any selection change/action, so the title's "every edit" is a hair broad, but the finding body states the trigger precisely. High severity stands — Cancel after a misclicked Delete or bad Import is unrecoverable.

title: Vault credential failures are silent — runs fall through to the wrong credentials with no user-visible warning
existing_state: VaultCredentialProvider.TryGetPassword swallows every exception (typo'd path, missing key, sealed Vault, expired auth, network down) into Debug.WriteLine and returns false (Services/Vault/VaultCredentialProvider.cs:59-63). Both consumers then silently fall back: Form1.GetHostConnections drops to the grid's username/password columns and then to any Credential-Manager-stored or toolbar password (Form1.cs:13332-13356), and the scheduler's BuildHostConnections does the same per-row fallback (Services/JobExecutionService.cs:512-532) while job-level Vault mode returns empty credentials with only a Debug.WriteLine (JobExecutionService.cs:639-640). Result: a one-character typo in a vault_path cell means SSH proceeds against 200 network devices using a stale or default identity. Nothing appears in the output panel, history, or status bar to indicate Vault was attempted and failed.
recommendation: Thread the failure reason out of the provider (an out string error or a result object) and surface it: (1) emit a warning line per host into the output panel/run log ('vault_path "secret/neta/sw-12" failed: permission denied — falling back to grid credentials'); (2) add a pre-run validation pass that resolves all distinct vault_paths once and shows a summary dialog if any fail, with an option to abort; (3) for jobs, record the warning into JobRunResult/host output so job history shows why auth used the wrong identity. Optionally add a config toggle 'treat vault_path failure as host failure' for environments with TACACS/AD lockout policies.
user_benefit: Prevents the worst multi-host failure mode: spraying wrong credentials at a fleet (which can trip account-lockout policies on network gear) and then debugging mystery auth failures with zero evidence that Vault was even consulted.

evidence.note: catch-all to Debug.WriteLine, returns false
failed vault lookup falls through to grid/stored/toolbar credentials
scheduler mirrors the silent fallback; Vault mode returns empty creds with debug-only warning

mockup_idea: Before/after of the run output panel: before — bare 'Authentication failed' lines per host; after — an amber pre-run banner 'Vault: 3 of 200 vault_path lookups failed (secret/neta/sw-12: permission denied, ...) — Continue with fallback credentials / Abort run'.

verification.notes: Core claim confirmed: VaultCredentialProvider swallows all failures into Debug.WriteLine (discarding VaultService's detailed VaultException messages), and per-host vault_path failures silently fall back to grid/stored/toolbar credentials in both Form1.GetHostConnections and the scheduler's BuildHostConnections with nothing in the output panel, status bar, or history — the fleet-spray scenario is real. One material error: job-level CredentialMode.Vault failure is NOT silent — ExecuteJobCoreAsync (JobExecutionService.cs:387-393) throws "Cannot resolve credentials for job '...' (mode: Vault)", which surfaces via OnJobFailed into JobStateChanged and a failed JobRunResult in job history (lines 909-927); the job aborts instead of running with wrong credentials, though the underlying Vault reason is still lost. Severity high remains justified by the per-host paths. Add for context: JobExecutionService.cs:387-393 (empty-cred guard throws) and 909-927 (OnJobFailed surfaces job-level Vault failure).]

title: localcmd confirmation prompts storm multi-host runs and loops; approval cannot be scoped to the run
existing_state: Unless `confirm: never`, every localcmd execution checks approval keyed to the exact RESOLVED command text plus a single approved host slot (Services/Scripting/Commands/LocalCmdCommand.cs:112-125). Two consequences: (1) a command containing {{item}} or {{Host_IP}} resolves differently each iteration, so a foreach re-prompts every single pass even after clicking 'Run Same Command' (the dialog's own scope label admits this: UI/LocalCmdConfirmationDialog.cs:73); (2) multi-host runs construct a fresh ScriptContext per host (Services/SshExecutionService.cs:1542, 1676, 1736), so approval state can never carry across hosts — a 200-host preset with one localcmd step produces 200 modal prompts that each pause the run. The only escape is `confirm: never` in the YAML, which permanently removes the guardrail. The dialog's three buttons are Run / Run Same Command / Cancel (LocalCmdConfirmationDialog.cs:80-120); there is no 'approve for this run' option.
recommendation: Add a run-scoped approval keyed to step identity rather than resolved text: a fourth dialog option 'Run for all hosts (this step, this run)' that records the StepPath or un-substituted command template in a run-level approval store owned by SshExecutionService and injected into each per-host ScriptContext via ConfigureScriptExecutionContext (the same place the confirmation provider is wired, SshExecutionService.cs:305-343). Keep the existing exact-text option for the cautious path. Show the resolved command preview in the dialog as today so the operator still sees what the template expands to on the current host.
user_benefit: A fleet operator can approve a vetted local command once and let the 200-host run proceed unattended, instead of either babysitting 200 dialogs or stripping the confirmation safety net out of the script with confirm: never.

evidence.note: approval keyed to exact resolved command + single LocalCmdApprovedHost slot
fresh ScriptContext per host — approval state never crosses hosts
scope label documents the narrow approval; only Run / Run Same Command / Cancel buttons exist

mockup_idea: The Local Command Confirmation dialog with a new scope row: radio/buttons 'Run once' / 'Run for all hosts this run' / 'Cancel', plus a subtitle showing 'Template: ping {{Host_IP}} — resolves to: ping 10.0.3.17 on this host', making the template-vs-resolved distinction visible.

verification.notes: Traced fully and every cited line holds verbatim. Approval is keyed to the resolved command text + a single approved-host slot (LocalCmdCommand.cs:112-125), so "Run Same Command" cannot survive {{item}} substitution; approval state lives in per-ScriptContext shared state and the sequential multi-host loop (SshExecutionService.cs:584-597) builds a fresh ScriptContext per host at exactly 1542/1676/1736 (preconnect path also per-host at 1880), so N hosts = N modal prompts. The finding is actually slightly understated: unattended/scheduled runs preflight-fail any localcmd that is not confirm:never (TryBuildUnattendedLocalCmdPreflightMessage, lines 541/937/1134), further forcing the guardrail off; ScriptContext.ResetLocalCmdApproval exists but has no callers, confirming no run-scoped mechanism exists.

title: Interactive terminal keyboard/clipboard gaps: F1-F12 never reach the host, Ctrl+Shift+C sends SIGINT, paste is right-click-only and multi-line paste executes instantly
existing_state: The terminal's key handler maps only Enter/Tab/Backspace/Escape/arrows/Home/End/PageUp/Down/Insert/Delete to Rebex FunctionKeys (Forms/InteractiveTerminalForm.cs:303-320); F1-F12 fall through `_ => null` and are silently dropped (:322-323), so full-screen TUI apps that depend on the F-bar (htop, mc, FortiGate menus) are unusable. The Ctrl+letter branch (:290-301) matches e.Control without excluding Shift and sends only ConsoleModifiers.Control — so the de-facto terminal copy shortcut Ctrl+Shift+C transmits a raw Ctrl+C (SIGINT) to the remote host, potentially killing whatever is running, and Ctrl+Shift+V sends Ctrl+V. There is no keyboard copy/paste at all: copy is select-to-copy on mouse-up only (UI/InteractiveTerminalViewportControl.cs:298-317), paste is right-click only (InteractiveTerminalForm.cs:379-385 → PasteClipboardToHost :449-467), Shift+Insert is forwarded to the host as an Insert keystroke (:317, 326-335), and a multi-line clipboard is normalized CRLF→LF (:481-486) and sent in one Send(text) call (Services/Terminal/InteractiveTerminalService.cs:1790-1803) — every line executes immediately on the remote device with no confirmation or bracketed-paste safety.
recommendation: In InteractiveTerminalForm_KeyDown: (1) add Keys.F1..F12 → Rebex FunctionKey.F1..F12 to the switch; (2) before the Ctrl+letter branch, intercept Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Insert (copy selection) and Ctrl+Shift+V / Shift+Insert (PasteClipboardToHost) so they never leak to the host; (3) in PasteClipboardToHost, when the normalized text contains a newline, show a small themed confirm (line count + first-line preview, 'Paste 14 lines?', don't-ask-again option) mirroring Windows Terminal's multi-line paste warning. Optionally honor bracketed paste mode when the remote application has enabled it.
user_benefit: Function-key-driven remote apps become usable, the most common terminal muscle-memory shortcut stops accidentally interrupting running commands on production hosts, and blind-executing a 30-line clipboard against a router becomes impossible.

verification.notes: Traced end-to-end and all claims hold: the KeyDown switch (Forms/InteractiveTerminalForm.cs:303-323) has no F1-F12 mappings so they are silently dropped; the Ctrl+letter branch (:290-301) matches Ctrl+Shift+C and discards Shift, and the service handler (Services/Terminal/InteractiveTerminalService.cs:1838) sends it as raw Ctrl+C to the host; paste is right-click only (:379-385, :449-467) with CRLF→LF normalization (:481-486) sent in one stream.Send (:1790-1803), so every embedded newline executes with no confirmation; Shift+Insert is forwarded to the host as Insert (:317, :326-335). Only nit: copy also fires on double-click word-select (viewport :275), not solely mouse-up — immaterial. KeyPreview=true and the absence of ProcessCmdKey/shortcut intercepts mean nothing prevents the SIGINT leak.

title: Terminal connection loss or errors close the window silently — no message, no reconnect
existing_state: When the SSH connection drops, the Rebex Disconnected/ActionRequested(DisconnectRequest) handlers just call RequestCloseSafe(form) (Services/Terminal/InteractiveTerminalService.cs:1687-1704) — the window vanishes with zero explanation. Worse, every error message the service tries to show ('[interactive-error] {ex.Message}' at InteractiveTerminalService.cs:1037, 1940, 2123, 2246, routed through AppendOutputSafe at 3281-3305) lands in InteractiveTerminalForm.AppendOutput, which is a documented no-op (Forms/InteractiveTerminalForm.cs:168-172: 'intentionally kept as a no-op'). So a pump failure, auth hiccup mid-session, or network blip all present identically: the terminal just disappears. There is no reconnect affordance anywhere in the terminal subsystem.
recommendation: On disconnect or pump error in window mode, stop closing the form: switch it to the already-existing detached read-only mode (EnableDetachedReadOnlyMode, Forms/InteractiveTerminalForm.cs:194-214) preserving the final screen, and add a thin status strip at the bottom showing 'Connection lost: <reason>' (route the [interactive-error] strings there instead of the no-op AppendOutput). For separate-mode sessions add a [Reconnect] button that re-runs ConnectAndLogin + startup negotiation and resumes the pump; shared-mode can show 'Session ended — close window' since the pooled session owns reconnection. Keep auto-close only for the unattended capture (show_window:false) path.
user_benefit: Operators on flaky management networks stop losing their place and wondering whether the app crashed; they see why the session ended and can reconnect in place instead of re-running the whole script.

evidence.note: Disconnected/DisconnectRequest handlers immediately RequestCloseSafe(form) with no user-visible message

title: A misspelled function name silently becomes a literal string in set: expressions — no parse-time or runtime signal
existing_state: Unknown-function handling is inconsistent by context. In condition position (if:/while:/assert:), ExpressionParser.ResolveFunction throws FormatException('Unknown function: ...') at runtime (Services/Scripting/ExpressionParser.cs:422-437). ScriptParser validation warns about unknown YAML keys (ScriptParser.cs:1151-1152 and ~15 similar sites) but performs zero function-name checking, so neither the editor's validation pass nor the Flow Canvas catches the typo before a run. The same silent philosophy runs through the library: int() parse-fail → 0, date_add unknown unit → input unchanged (DateTimeFunctions.cs:102), count() with an unparseable lambda degrades to a plain count (CollectionFunctions.cs:130-131).
recommendation: Add a function-name lint to the existing ScriptParser validation pass: scan set: expressions and condition strings for name(...) patterns (TryParseFunctionCall at JsonUtilities.cs:567 already does the parsing) and check each name against a unified known-function set (registry + legacy switch names + json.* methods — the same metadata table as the autocomplete work in UX-024). Surface misses through the same warning channel as 'Unknown step key', with a did-you-mean suggestion (edit distance catches uper→upper, indexof→index_of). user_benefit: Today a one-letter typo produces a literal 'uper(host)' string sent to live network gear with no error anywhere; users discover it from device output. Catching it at validation, like unknown step keys already are, turns a silent field failure into a squiggle in the editor.

title: Checked hosts with invalid Host_IP values are silently dropped from runs — no error, no result, mismatched counts
existing_state: Invalid hosts are dropped silently at two layers. The service then skips again: ExecuteAsync continues past invalid hosts producing no ExecutionResult (SshExecutionService.cs:394-395 and 439-443, the latter logging only to debug), the script path does the same (:589-591), and ExecuteFolderAsync filters them out up front (hosts.Where(h => h.IsValid()), :634) even after the user explicitly checked those hosts in the run dialog. title: Grid passwords are silently moved to Windows Credential Manager — invisible to the user, not gated on the setting, and unmanageable afterward
existing_state: Two silent flows move grid passwords into Windows Credential Manager. (1) On environment load, any non-empty 'password' cell is stored and the cell is blanked with zero notification (Form1.cs:2284-2304; same migration in MigratePasswordsToCredentialManager, Form1.cs:1501-1523) — a user who authored per-host passwords in their CSV sees them disappear, and a subsequent Save writes the password column back empty, so the file shared with a teammate no longer works. The password column tooltip (Form1.cs:134-141) never mentions this. (2) At run time, any password typed into the grid is auto-saved under SSH_Helper:host:{host}|user:{user} the moment a run builds connections (Form1.cs:13346-13352) and auto-loaded whenever the cell is empty (:13353-13356) — gated only on provider availability (IsCredentialManagerAvailable, Form1.cs:1368), NOT on the Credentials.UseCredentialManager setting, which defaults to false and gates only the default password (Models/AppConfiguration.cs:564-570). There is no UI anywhere to enumerate or delete per-host entries; only the default password has a clear path (Form1.cs:1474-1480). Consequences: 'I cleared the password but it still connects' confusion, and after a fleet-wide password rotation hundreds of stale per-host entries keep being auto-injected until each one fails, with no bulk-clear short of Windows' credential applet.
recommendation: Three parts: (1) make the migration visible — after moving N passwords during environment load, show a status-bar message ('Moved 3 passwords to Windows Credential Manager; cells cleared') plus a one-time themed dialog with a don't-show-again checkbox, and update the password column tooltip; (2) honor a setting — reuse Credentials.UseCredentialManager or add a dedicated 'Remember per-host passwords' toggle at the StoreHostPassword/TryResolveHostPassword call sites so the behavior is opt-in; (3) add a 'Stored Credentials...' manager (Settings > Credentials or Tools menu) listing this app's credential targets (host/user pairs, job creds, default) with per-row delete and 'Clear all host passwords' — CredentialTargets (Services/Credentials/CredentialTargets.cs) already centralizes the naming scheme; add a CredEnumerate P/Invoke with the SSH_Helper* filter.
user_benefit: Operators regain control and visibility over where secrets actually live; password rotations become a one-click cleanup instead of a hunt through Windows' credential applet; and 'where did my CSV passwords go?' stops being a discovered-the-hard-way surprise.

existing_state: Settings exposes a 'Prefer SSH agent when available' checkbox (SettingsDialog.cs:459, persisted at 2675) and the value is plumbed into both the execution service and the pool (Form1.cs:358, 5732). But TryLoginWithAgent unconditionally returns false in both places — SshExecutionService.cs:2855-2868 ('The current SSH library does not expose agent-backed authentication APIs') and SshConnectionPool.cs:689-697 — so every connection silently falls back to key/password. The fallback notice is debug-mode-only (SshDebugLog at 2862/2867). Agent detection also only checks SSH_AUTH_SOCK/SSH_AGENT_PID env vars (2871-2879), which Windows OpenSSH-agent and Pageant users typically don't have set anyway. A user who enables this believes their key never leaves the agent while the app is actually using stored passwords/key files.
recommendation: Short term (S): make the UI honest — disable the checkbox with a '(not supported by the current SSH library)' suffix, or show an inline warning when checked, and remove the dead plumbing. Longer term (L, separate decision): implement real agent auth against the Windows OpenSSH agent named pipe (\\.\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent) / Pageant shared-memory protocol and have the agent perform signing, falling back as today.
user_benefit: Removes a misleading security setting: users no longer believe agent-held keys are in use when they aren't, and the eventual real implementation lets keys stay in the agent instead of as passphrase-protected files on disk.

title: Failed shell-prompt detection is silent; runs degrade into a per-command 60-second timeout slog
existing_state: SshShellSession.InitializeAsync (Services/SshShellSession.cs:279-310) retries prompt detection up to 3 times, but when no prompt is ever detected it only emits a debug-mode-only warning ('WARNING: Could not detect a valid shell prompt after all attempts', :303-307) and returns normally. Execution then proceeds: each subsequent command waits on generic prompt patterns and typically dies by the per-command CommandTimeout (default 60s, Services/SshTimeoutOptions.cs). On a device with an unusual prompt (long prompts >80 chars and quote-heavy prompts are rejected by PromptDetector heuristics, Utilities/PromptDetector.cs:174, 190), a 10-command preset means ~10 minutes of consecutive timeout errors, and nothing in the output tells the user the root cause is prompt detection rather than the commands or the network. The excellent diagnostics that do exist (line-by-line prompt-match autopsy, SshShellSession.cs:893-921) are gated behind Debug mode, which the user has no reason to enable because nothing pointed them there.
recommendation: When InitializeAsync ends with _currentPrompt empty, emit a visible warning line through the normal OutputReceived stream (e.g. '[WARNING] Could not detect a shell prompt on <host> — commands may time out. Enable Debug Mode (menu) for prompt diagnostics.') and set a flag on the session; when a subsequent command then times out, prefix the timeout error with 'no shell prompt was detected during connection' so the failure is attributed correctly. Optionally add a config toggle to fail fast instead of attempting commands.
user_benefit: Turns the single most confusing failure mode on nonstandard devices (every command times out, no explanation) into a one-line diagnosis that also points the user at the existing Debug Mode tooling.

Two description errors: (1) after failed detection the read loop falls back to the generic pattern ^.+[#$>%→❯➜]\s*$ (:202/:123, matched at :848), which still matches the finding's own examples (>80-char and quote-heavy prompts ending in #/$/>), so those produce premature/odd matches rather than timeouts — the 60s-per-command slog only hits prompts with no standard trailing terminator, a narrower trigger; (2) timeouts emit no error at all (ReadUntilPromptWithPolling breaks at :761-764 and returns output as success), so the symptom is silent 60s stalls with missing output, not "consecutive timeout errors" — which actually strengthens the case for the recommended attribution line. title: while/repeat hitting max_iterations reports success — runaway loops truncate work silently
existing_state: Both loop commands hardcode DefaultMaxIterations = 10000 (Services/Scripting/Commands/WhileCommand.cs:14, RepeatCommand.cs:15). When the cap is reached they emit a single Warning-type output line and return Success (WhileCommand.cs:105-110 returns {Success = true}; RepeatCommand.cs:85-90 likewise). A while whose condition never flips — e.g. polling a device that never comes back, or a typo'd variable that makes the condition perpetually true — therefore stops mid-work and the run, job history, and any notify-on-failure logic all see a green result. The per-step max_iterations override exists (WhileCommand.cs:30-32, RepeatCommand.cs:31-33) but there is no way to make cap-exhaustion fail the step.
recommendation: Add an on_max_iterations: fail | warn option on while/repeat (and foreach if it shares the pattern). Defaulting to fail is the honest behavior; if back-compat matters, keep warn as default but emit it as Error-type output and set a _loop_truncated context variable plus a flag on CommandResult so the Flow Canvas run summary and job history can show 'loop hit cap' instead of a clean pass. The change is localized to the two cap checks.
user_benefit: A stuck polling loop in an overnight scheduled job becomes a red failed run with a clear reason, instead of a green run that quietly did 10,000 useless iterations and skipped everything after the real work was supposed to happen.

title: Invalid numeric step options (timeout: 30s, retry: two) are silently discarded by the parser
existing_state: The step-root option parser drops any value that fails int.TryParse without recording an error or warning: `timeout` (Services/Scripting/ScriptParser.cs:979-982), `retry` (988-991), `retry_delay` (992-996), and `max_iterations` (1000-1004) all use `if (int.TryParse(...)) step.X = ...;` with no else branch. A user who writes `timeout: 30s` or `retry_delay: 1.5` gets a script that validates green and runs with the option simply absent — the global default timeout applies and they never learn why their per-step timeout 'didn't work'. This contrasts sharply with the rest of the parser, which produces line-accurate did-you-mean errors for unknown keys.
recommendation: In each of the four cases, on TryParse failure add a ParseError with the line number and offending value (matching the existing error style), e.g. 'Line 14: timeout must be an integer number of seconds (got 30s)'. While there, accept the obvious duration suffixes users keep reaching for — parse 30s/2m/1h into seconds for timeout/retry_delay — which both fixes the trap and adds the ergonomics everyone expects from modern tools.
user_benefit: A timeout or retry the user believes is configured but silently isn't is exactly the kind of trap that surfaces as a 3 a.m. hung fleet run; this makes the mistake impossible to miss and the natural syntax just work.

title: Cancel and on_error: continue mean different things in every interactive/file command — and confirm cannot be cancelled at all
existing_state: Pressing Cancel in a script prompt does a different thing depending on which command opened it: readfile's picker aborts the entire run via CommandResult.Exit(ScriptExitStatus.Cancelled) (Services/Scripting/Commands/ReadFileCommand.cs:360-370); input, choose, and multiselect return a plain step Fail bypassing ApplyOnError even though their other failures honor on_error: continue (InputCommand.cs:61-65/82, ChooseCommand.cs:58-62/78, MultiselectCommand.cs:56-60); writefile's save dialog returns Fail, or Suppressed under on_error: continue (WriteFileCommand.cs:42-51). Meanwhile `confirm` offers no cancel path at all: ESC and window-close map to the No button (ConfirmCommand.cs:114 CancelButton = btnNo), so the script always proceeds with the literal string 'false' stored (ConfirmCommand.cs:41-42) — an operator who wants to abort the run at a confirmation gate cannot express that from the dialog. on_error: continue is equally inconsistent: readfile and writefile path/extension validation errors return CommandResult.Ok(message) — plain success, not even flagged as suppressed (ReadFileCommand.cs:62-65, 84-87, 95-98; WriteFileCommand.cs:58-59) — while every other command goes through ApplyOnError → Suppressed; and playsound silently treats an omitted on_error as continue (PlaySoundCommand.cs:127-134), documented only in a code comment. Finally, the unattended-run dialog gate exists only in readfile (AllowFileSelectionDialogs check, ReadFileCommand.cs:237-238); writefile with a relative path pops its modal save dialog unconditionally (WriteFileCommand.cs:175-182), so a scheduled job stalls on an invisible dialog.
recommendation: Define one contract and apply it across the commands: (1) Cancel produces one consistent result — e.g. Fail with a 'cancelled by user' message routed through ApplyOnError, plus an optional per-step on_cancel: fail|exit|continue for scripts that want the readfile abort-the-run behavior, and a <into>_cancelled marker variable so scripts can branch; (2) give confirm an optional allow_cancel: true that adds a Cancel button distinct from No, failing the step under the same contract (register the key in the parser tables, ScriptParser.cs:138); (3) every on_error: continue path returns CommandResult.Suppressed (route through ApplyOnError), never bare Ok, so _last_error and the canvas suppressed-error styling work; (4) gate writefile's save dialog on context.AllowFileSelectionDialogs like readfile; (5) make playsound's continue-by-default explicit in docs/validator.
user_benefit: Script authors can predict what Cancel and on_error: continue actually do instead of learning per-command folklore, operators get a real 'abort here' affordance at confirmation gates, and scheduled jobs stop stalling on invisible save dialogs.

existing_state: The Scintilla autocomplete provider (Services/Editor/ScriptAutocompleteProvider.cs) completes step commands (lines 116-161), top-level keys (163-178), required option keys (180-217), built-in symbols like _output/_prompt (92-104, 219-231), and host columns — but not one of the ~112 scripting functions (grep for regex_match/date_add/base64/ip_in_cidr across the file: zero matches). title: Find is fragmented: Ctrl+F always targets the output pane, the find bar is permanently dark, the run-output viewer reimplements search, and the script editor has no find at all
existing_state: Form1.ProcessCmdKey intercepts Ctrl+F app-wide and always opens the output find anchored to txtOutput (Form1.cs:14462-14464, 14482-14492); the find logic is hardwired to txtOutput (seeds from txtOutput.SelectedText at 14484, match/cursor logic at 14516, 14549), and F3/Shift+F3 are likewise always captured for output-pane navigation (14472-14477). title: Settings dialog is a fixed 544x620 box for ~80 settings — not resizable, 430px hardcoded rows, and font auto-scaling deliberately suppressed
existing_state: SettingsDialog is FormBorderStyle.FixedDialog at 544x620 with MaximizeBox disabled (SettingsDialog.cs:211-216), even though the tab control already carries full four-way resize anchors that are dead code under the fixed border (219-224). The dialog declares AutoScaleMode.Font (208-209), but Form1 then applies the user's configured dialog font through DialogTheme.SetDialogFont (Form1.cs:5718), which intentionally flips AutoScaleMode to None (UI/DialogTheme.cs:522-529) — so when a user raises the UI font size (a feature this app prominently offers), the text grows but the 544x620 shell and absolutely-positioned rows do not, clipping labels and controls. The Vault and Notifications detail panes hardcode every row to Width = 430 (e.g. SettingsDialog.cs:543-551, 576-642) — long Vault addresses, namespaces, and SMTP recipient lists get cramped single-line boxes — and the Appearance tab packs 13 font spinners plus a live preview into a scrolling panel. Contrast: EnvironmentDialog in the same app is sizable with persisted geometry in WindowState (EnvironmentDialog.cs:66-75, 303-323). There is also no way to find a setting — six tabs must be hunted through manually.
recommendation: Switch to FormBorderStyle.Sizable with MinimumSize = current 544x620, and persist geometry to WindowState exactly as EnvironmentDialog does (the tab control's existing anchors then start working for free). Replace the hardcoded 430px Vault/Notification rows with Dock=Top / TableLayoutPanel rows that grow with the dialog and reflow at larger fonts instead of clipping. As a follow-up, add a small filter TextBox above the tab control that hides non-matching rows across tabs (each setting row already has a label to match against) — the VS Code settings-search pattern.
user_benefit: Users with long Vault URLs, multi-recipient SMTP lists, high-DPI displays, or enlarged fonts (the audience the app's own font settings target) stop fighting a cramped, clipping fixed window; a settings filter cuts 'which tab was that on?' time to zero.

evidence.note: FixedDialog 544x620; AutoScaleMode.Font declared; tab anchors dead under fixed border
SetDialogFont assigns user font with AutoScaleMode.None — layout never scales with font
Vault detail rows/panels hardcoded Width=430
In-house precedent: sizable dialog with geometry persisted to WindowState

mockup_idea: Before/after pair: 'before' = the current cramped 544px dialog at 125% font with a truncated Vault address field and a scrollbar on the Appearance tab; 'after' = the same dialog stretched to ~900x700 with full-width reflowed fields, no scrolling, and a 'Search settings…' filter box above the tabs showing 'timeout' filtering down to 3 highlighted rows.

verification.notes: Every cited fact traced exactly: FixedDialog 544x620 with dead four-way tab anchors (SettingsDialog.cs:208-224), SetDialogFont deliberately suppressing auto-scale (DialogTheme.cs:522-529, applied to this dialog at Form1.cs:5718 with the user-configurable DialogFontSize), 17 hardcoded Width=430 rows/panels across the Vault and Notifications tabs, 13 font spinners + live preview in a scrolling Appearance panel, six tabs with no search/filter, and the sizable+persisted EnvironmentDialog precedent (66-78, 303-323). Only quibble: initial DPI scaling does work at construction via AutoScaleMode.Font, so the high-DPI audience mention is slightly overbroad — the clipping is specific to user-enlarged dialog fonts, which is the finding's core claim anyway. Medium severity (real friction, no data loss) is right.

title: Job Import preview: no Select All/None, broken-target jobs are checked by default, and conflicts are rename-only
existing_state: ImportPreviewDialog adds every row with the Import checkbox forced to true — including rows flagged 'Target folder/preset not found - will be disabled' (ImportPreviewDialog.cs:244-249 adds true unconditionally; MissingTarget status at 231-237). Name conflicts are presented as a fait accompli: 'Renamed (original: X)' (226-230) with the Name column read-only (81-87) — no way to overwrite the existing job or pick a different name from the preview.
recommendation: Three small upgrades to the same grid: (1) add Select All / Select None LinkLabels (or a tri-state header checkbox via HeaderCell replacement) above the grid, wired to the existing UpdateSummaryLabel; (2) default-uncheck rows where entry.MissingTarget is true and tint the whole row so broken imports are opt-in; (3) make the Name cell editable for conflicted rows, writing back to entry.ResolvedName with a duplicate-name check, and optionally a per-row Rename / Overwrite / Skip choice in the Status column.
user_benefit: Importing job bundles between machines (the whole point of export/import) stops being a click-fest, and users no longer accidentally accept disabled, broken jobs or forced renames they never saw.

title: Job import failures all collapse to 'No valid jobs found' — corrupt file, wrong format, and empty export are indistinguishable
existing_state: JobExportService.ImportFromFile and ImportFromString wrap everything in catch-all blocks that return an empty list (Services/JobExportService.cs:71-86 and 92-107): unreadable file, malformed JSON, a non-.sshjobs JSON file, a clipboard string that isn't a GZip+Base64 export blob, and a genuinely empty export all produce the identical result. JobListDialog.ProcessImportedJobs then shows the single generic message 'No valid jobs found in the import data.' (JobListDialog.cs:1420-1427). A teammate who pastes the wrong clipboard content or picks the wrong file gets no clue whether the data was bad, the format was wrong, or the export really contained nothing — contrast with the same dialog's export path, which does surface the real exception (JobListDialog.cs:1166-1170).
recommendation: Change the two import methods to return a small result type (Jobs + ErrorKind/ErrorMessage) or throw typed exceptions caught at the call sites. Distinguish at minimum: file not found / not readable, JSON parse failure ('not a valid .sshjobs file'), decode failure ('clipboard does not contain an SSH Helper job export'), unsupported Version, and genuinely zero jobs. Surface the specific message in ProcessImportedJobs's warning dialog.
user_benefit: When sharing jobs between teammates' machines — the entire point of .sshjobs/clipboard export — a failed import tells the user what actually went wrong instead of gaslighting them about an 'empty' file.

evidence.note: catch { return new List<JobDefinition>(); } on both import paths
Single generic 'No valid jobs found in the import data.' for every failure mode

verification.notes: Traced fully and accurate: both import methods (JobExportService.cs:71-86, 92-107) collapse missing file, bad JSON, non-export JSON, bad clipboard blob, and empty export into identical empty lists (the test suite codifies this), and ProcessImportedJobs (JobListDialog.cs:1420-1427) shows the one generic message while export surfaces real exceptions (1166-1170). Worth noting: both import call sites already contain specific catch handlers ("Could not read job file: ...", "Could not parse clipboard data: ...", JobListDialog.cs:1215-1218/1237-1240) that are unreachable for data errors because the service swallows them — the distinguished-error UI plumbing exists but is dead, making the recommended fix even smaller than stated. title: Choose prompt dialog has no search/filter and a fixed 10-row, non-resizable list
existing_state: The `choose` script command shows a plain ListBox capped at 10 visible rows (Services/Scripting/Commands/ChooseCommand.cs:112, visibleItems = Math.Min(options.Count, 10)) inside a FixedDialog form (ChooseCommand.cs:119) — no filter box, no type-ahead beyond the ListBox's default first-letter jump, no resizing. Options are frequently runtime data: options: accepts a variable reference or list resolved via ChoiceOptionResolver (ChooseCommand.cs:35-39), so scripts routinely feed it host lists, interfaces, VLANs, or extracted device output. Picking one entry out of 200 hosts means scrolling a 10-row viewport with a mouse.
recommendation: Add a filter TextBox above the ListBox in ScriptChooseDialog (ChooseCommand.cs:97-225): live substring filtering of _options into the ListBox (keep a filtered-index map so SelectedValue still resolves to the right ChoiceOption), Enter in the filter accepts when one item remains, and keystrokes typed while the list has focus route into the filter. Make the form resizable (FormBorderStyle.Sizable with a sensible MinimumSize) and anchor the list. Apply the same pattern to the multiselect dialog, which shares ChoiceOptionResolver plumbing.
user_benefit: Selecting from realistic option lists (hundreds of hosts/interfaces) becomes a two-keystroke operation instead of a scroll hunt — the standard set by every command palette and SecureCRT's session picker.

verification.notes: Traced fully: ScriptChooseDialog caps the list at 10 rows (ChooseCommand.cs:112), uses FixedDialog with no anchoring or resize (line 119, fixed Size), and contains no filter TextBox or type-ahead beyond the stock ListBox first-letter jump. title: Notification profiles cannot be tested from Settings — Vault gets a Test Connection button, notifications get nothing
existing_state: The Vault settings tab has a 'Test Connection' button that exercises the in-dialog values end-to-end (SettingsDialog.cs:731). title: Run start blocks the UI thread on sequential per-host Vault reads; an expired OIDC token pops a surprise synchronous browser login
existing_state: ExecutePresetOnRowsAsync builds host connections synchronously on the UI thread (Form1.cs:12277 — it shows owned dialogs immediately after at :12286-12288, confirming UI-thread context). For each row with a vault_path, GetHostConnections calls VaultCredentialProvider.TryGetPassword, which is sync-over-async (.GetAwaiter().GetResult(), Services/Vault/VaultCredentialProvider.cs:48-49) — one blocking Vault HTTP round-trip per distinct secret path (the 300s cache only helps repeated paths). With 200 devices holding per-device secrets, the app freezes for the full sequential resolution before the run even begins, with no progress indication. Worse: if the profile uses OIDC and the cached token has expired, the first lookup launches a full interactive browser login (VaultService.GetAuthenticatedProfileAsync → AuthenticateWithOidcAsync → VaultOidcLoginFlow opens the system browser and blocks on an HttpListener, Services/Vault/VaultOidcLoginFlow.cs:42-69) — the user gets an unexplained browser window while the main window is frozen for up to OidcTimeoutSeconds (default 180s). The same sync-over-async pattern exists in inline {{vault:}} (ScriptContext.cs:748) and vault() functions (VaultFunctions.cs:36).
recommendation: Make credential resolution an async pre-run phase: extract the vault portion of GetHostConnections into an awaited 'resolve credentials' step that (1) runs off the UI thread with bounded parallelism across distinct paths, (2) shows progress in the status bar ('Resolving Vault credentials 38/142...'), and (3) pre-flights authentication once — if the OIDC token is expired, show an explicit 'Vault login required' prompt before opening the browser instead of letting it appear mid-freeze. The interactive-terminal path already resolves per-row inside an async lambda (Form1.cs:8916), so the per-row resolution is already separable.
user_benefit: No more multi-second (or 3-minute) frozen main window at the exact moment the operator clicks Run, and no more mystery browser windows — the app explains what it needs (a Vault login) before taking over the screen.

evidence.note: GetHostConnections enumerated synchronously on the UI thread at run start
sync-over-async Vault read per row
expired OIDC token triggers a blocking interactive browser flow, timeout default 180s

verification.notes: Every cited location is accurate (sync per-row Vault reads via .GetAwaiter().GetResult() materialized on the UI thread at Form1.cs:12277; per-path 300s cache; OIDC browser flow with 180s default; same pattern at ScriptContext.cs:748/VaultFunctions.cs:36) and the recommended async pre-run phase is not implemented. However, the described behavior is understated on this exact path: VaultService has no ConfigureAwait(false), so the first uncached read under the WinForms SynchronizationContext is a classic sync-over-async deadlock (permanent hang — sibling finding BUG-002), meaning the "sequential 200-host freeze then run" and "browser pops while frozen" sequences cannot actually complete on the Run-click path (the OIDC deadlock hits at the auth_url HTTP await at VaultService.cs:492 before the browser opens); the surprise-browser scenario is real only on the background script-execution paths. The recommendation remains the right fix — treat this as the UX companion to BUG-002, which should be fixed together.

title: Missing WebView2 runtime surfaces as a raw exception message instead of install guidance (Flow Canvas and Run Output window)
existing_state: If CoreWebView2Environment.CreateAsync / EnsureCoreWebView2Async fails (most commonly WebView2RuntimeNotFoundException on machines without the Evergreen runtime — enterprise images, Server SKUs), FlowCanvasForm shows only `Error: {ex.Message}` in the status label with detail going to Debug.WriteLine (UI/FlowCanvasForm.cs:101-106; the throwing calls are at :109-130), and RunOutputWindowForm has the identical pattern (UI/RunOutputWindowForm.cs:83-88). The runtime's exception message is cryptic and offers no next step, leaving both the flagship visual editor and the detached output window dead with no explanation. This contrasts sharply with the same form's missing-dist diagnostics, which list every searched path and give dev/publish remediation steps (UI/FlowCanvasForm.cs:183-191). There is no startup probe either: the user discovers the problem only when opening the canvas.
recommendation: In both forms' init catch blocks, special-case Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.WebView2RuntimeNotFoundException (and check CoreWebView2Environment.GetAvailableBrowserVersionString() up front) to show a message in the style of the dist-not-found text: 'Flow Canvas needs the Microsoft WebView2 Runtime' with a clickable link to https://developer.microsoft.com/microsoft-edge/webview2/ and a Retry button that re-runs InitializeWebView2Async. Factor the handler into a small shared helper since the two forms duplicate the init pattern; keep the generic ex.Message fallback for other exceptions.
user_benefit: On any machine without the Evergreen runtime, the user gets a fix-it-in-one-click path instead of a cryptic one-liner that makes the flagship editor look broken — cutting the most likely 'Flow Canvas is broken' support conversation to a 2-minute self-service install.

title: Canvas load failures are completely silent — blank or stale canvas with no error surface and no handshake watchdog
existing_state: Three independent failure modes all end in a blank or stale canvas with zero user-visible feedback. (1) Form1.LoadCurrentScriptIntoCanvas wraps TextToGraph in `catch { // Silently fail — canvas will show empty state }` (Form1.cs:6886-6889): a YAML preset that parses in the editor but trips the bridge shows an empty canvas on fresh open — or, worse, on the window-reuse path (Form1.cs:6648-6655) the canvas silently keeps the PREVIOUS preset's graph. (2) There is no watchdog on the ready handshake: if React crashes before posting {type:'ready'}, every message including load-graph queues forever in _pendingMessages (UI/FlowCanvasForm.cs:352-362) and the status label was already hidden by NavigationCompleted success (145-153), leaving a dead white window. (3) Malformed messages and handler exceptions are Debug.WriteLine-only (UI/FlowCanvasForm.cs:208-211, 306-309), invisible in release builds.
recommendation: In LoadCurrentScriptIntoCanvas's catch, send the canvas a visible error (the existing show-error/DialogTheme path or a dedicated load-error message rendered as a canvas banner) including ex.Message, and log via SshDebugLog. In FlowCanvasForm, start a ~10s timer after NavigationCompleted; if _reactReady is still false, re-show _statusLabel with 'Flow Canvas failed to start (press F12 for DevTools)' guidance. Route OnWebMessageReceived exceptions to the app debug log instead of Debug-only output.
user_benefit: When the canvas breaks (bad dist after an update, a script that hits a bridge edge case), the user currently has no way to distinguish 'my script is empty' from 'the canvas is broken' — and may edit/apply against a stale graph from a different preset. A 10-line watchdog and one error banner turn a support mystery into a self-explanatory state.

evidence.note: Swallow-all catch with 'Silently fail' comment
Reuse path: failed reload leaves the previous preset's graph on screen
Status label hidden on nav success; no ready timeout; messages queue forever
Message/handler exceptions Debug-only

mockup_idea: The canvas window in its failed state: today a plain empty surface; after, a centered card 'Couldn't load this preset into the canvas: <parser message>' with 'Open YAML editor' and 'Copy details' buttons, plus the startup-timeout variant of the same card.

verification.notes: All three failure modes verified at the cited lines: the swallow-all catch with the "Silently fail" comment (Form1.cs:6886-6889) is reachable because IsYamlScript is a heuristic line check while TextToGraph runs full ScriptParser.Parse (throws ScriptParseException, ScriptParser.cs:567/571); _reactReady has no timer/watchdog anywhere in FlowCanvasForm so messages queue forever after NavigationCompleted hides the status label; and both message-handler catches are Debug.WriteLine-only (compiled out in Release). The stale-graph exposure is actually broader than the finding states — LoadCurrentScriptIntoCanvas is also invoked on preset load (Form1.cs:2160) and preset save (Form1.cs:10221) while the canvas is open, so switching presets with a bridge failure silently leaves the prior preset's graph on screen.

title: Canvas Ctrl+F search never pans the viewport to the current match, and matches hidden internal metadata
existing_state: Enter/Shift+Enter in the search overlay (FlowCanvas/src/panels/SearchOverlay.tsx:28-34) call nextSearchResult/prevSearchResult, which only increment searchIndex modulo results (stores/slices/uiSlice.ts:246-260). App.tsx:280-317 applies 'search-match'/'search-current' classNames to nodes — and that is all: nothing calls setCenter/fitView, so on any graph larger than one screen the 'current' match is usually off-viewport and cycling results appears to do nothing. The codebase already has the exact pattern needed: ProblemsPanel.tsx:19-25 selects a node and setCenter-animates to it (reduced-motion aware). Separately, the match predicate includes JSON.stringify(data.props) (uiSlice.ts:236-239), and imported blocks carry hidden bridge metadata inside props — _stepPath like 'steps/3/then/0' is written for every step (Services/FlowCanvasBridge.cs:422) and _isChildOf/_branchColor/_yamlSnippet for branch children (FlowCanvasBridge.cs:743-746) — so queries like 'step', 'then', 'if', or a node id match blocks whose visible fields contain nothing of the sort, inflating the 'n of m' count with phantom hits.
recommendation: In SearchOverlay (or a store subscription on searchIndex/searchResults), look up the current match node and call reactFlow.setCenter(nodeCenterX, nodeCenterY, { zoom: Math.max(currentZoom, 0.75), duration: reducedMotion ? 0 : 300 }) — mirror ProblemsPanel.tsx:24. In uiSlice.setSearchQuery, build the props haystack from Object.entries(props).filter(([k]) => !k.startsWith('_')) and match against values only (not raw JSON with keys/braces). Optionally render a small result list under the search box (block label + type) for click-to-jump.
user_benefit: Search becomes usable on real-world presets (50+ blocks): hit Ctrl+F, type, Enter-cycle, and the canvas flies to each hit like VS Code or any node editor. Match counts stop lying about phantom hits from internal YAML snippets and layout metadata.

evidence.note: setSearchQuery stringifies full props (incl. _yamlSnippet/_stepPath); next/prev only mutate searchIndex
Enter cycles results, no viewport action
search results only become classNames; no setCenter/fitView
existing select+setCenter pattern to reuse

verification.notes: Traced fully: Enter/Shift+Enter (SearchOverlay.tsx:28-34) only bump searchIndex (uiSlice.ts:246-260), App.tsx:280-317 only assigns classNames, and the sole setCenter in all of FlowCanvas/src is ProblemsPanel.tsx:24 — so the current match is never panned into view. The phantom-hit claim also holds: uiSlice.ts:236 JSON.stringifies full props (keys included), and the bridge writes _stepPath/_isChildOf/_branchLabel/_branchColor into data.props (FlowCanvasBridge.cs:422, 743-748; attached at 453/762). title: Palette is a fixed scroll of ~38 blocks with no type-to-filter, collapse, or quick-add
existing_state: Palette.tsx renders all block definitions (38 'category:' entries in FlowCanvas/src/blockDefs/registry.ts) across 7 hardcoded categories (Palette.tsx:12-14) as one static scrolling column (Palette.tsx:55-105). title: Flow Canvas window forgets its position across app restarts (size is remembered, location isn't)
existing_state: FlowCanvasForm caches its location only in a static session field (UI/FlowCanvasForm.cs:31-32, 46-50, 77-81); SavePersistedSize persists width/height alone, and only from Dispose (518-534). Models/AppConfiguration.cs:499-500 has FlowCanvasWidth/Height but no Left/Top. So a user who parks the canvas on a second monitor gets it re-centered on the parent every app launch. The newer RunOutputWindowForm already does this right: it persists both size and location from FormClosing using last-Normal-state values (UI/RunOutputWindowForm.cs:45-47, 73, 215-240). Neither form clamps the restored position to current monitor bounds.
recommendation: Mirror RunOutputWindowForm in FlowCanvasForm: add WindowState.FlowCanvasLeft/Top, restore them in the ctor (session cache > persisted > CenterParent), and save geometry in FormClosing instead of Dispose. While there, add a Screen.AllScreens bounds clamp to both forms' restore paths so a saved position on a disconnected monitor snaps back on-screen.
user_benefit: Daily users with a two-monitor setup (the explicit target of the detachable Run Output work) stop re-dragging the canvas to its spot every session — table-stakes behavior for professional tools.

evidence.note: Session-only location; size-only persistence written in Dispose
Reference implementation: size+location persisted from FormClosing
Only FlowCanvasWidth/Height exist in WindowState

title: Custom-painted controls drop keyboard affordances: Stop All has no focus indicator, Presets/Favorites tabs are mouse-only
existing_state: FlatVisualButton's OnPaint draws background, border, and text only (UI/FlatVisualButton.cs:86-118) — no focus rectangle, and TextFormatFlags.NoPrefix (:117) strips mnemonic underlines; its single production use is btnStopAll (Form1.Designer.cs:132), the emergency Stop All button, so a keyboard user tabbing toward it gets no visual cue it is focused before pressing Space/Enter mid-run. PresetTabHeaderStrip (the main window's Presets/Favorites switcher) sets TabStop = false (UI/PresetTabHeaderStrip.cs:26) and handles only mouse events (:72-108) — there is no keyboard path to switch between Presets and Favorites at all.
recommendation: In FlatVisualButton.OnPaint, when Focused && ShowFocusCues draw ControlPaint.DrawFocusRectangle (or a 1px accent inner border to match the flat style) and drop NoPrefix so &-mnemonics render. For PresetTabHeaderStrip, set TabStop = true, override IsInputKey/OnKeyDown for Left/Right arrows to change SelectedIndex, and draw a focus underline; both are small additions to existing OnPaint code.
user_benefit: Keyboard-driven operators (common among terminal-heavy network engineers) can reliably hit Stop All under pressure and switch preset tabs without reaching for the mouse.

evidence.note: OnPaint: no focus cue; :117 NoPrefix strips mnemonics
btnStopAll is the sole FlatVisualButton
TabStop=false; mouse handlers only, no key handling

title: local_cmd confirmation dialog ignores font settings, is unthemed in light mode, and clips its widest button
existing_state: LocalCmdConfirmationForm — the safety gate shown when a YAML script wants to run a local command — is hand-laid-out in absolute pixels (UI/LocalCmdConfirmationDialog.cs:24-123) and never calls DialogTheme.SetDialogFont, so it ignores the user's configured dialog font that every other dialog honors. 'Run Same Command' is squeezed into a fixed 140px button (:96-98) and will clip at larger fonts/DPI. Theming is dark-only and gated on its own brightness heuristic (mainForm.BackColor.GetBrightness() < 0.2f, :125-126): in light mode the form gets no DialogTheme treatment at all (raised 3D buttons amid an app of flat styled ones), duplicating the detection logic DialogTheme already centralizes in ResolveDarkMode.
recommendation: Apply DialogTheme.SetDialogFont(this, DialogTheme-resolved font) and call StyleButton/ApplyTo unconditionally with the resolved darkMode (DialogTheme.ResolveDarkMode(owner)) instead of the local heuristic. Switch the button row to a right-anchored FlowLayoutPanel with AutoSize buttons so 'Run Same Command' never clips. This is the dialog a user reads before approving arbitrary local command execution — it should look trustworthy.
user_benefit: The one dialog asking the user to approve local command execution stops looking like an unfinished afterthought and stays readable at the user's chosen font size.

evidence.note: absolute pixel layout, no SetDialogFont, 140px 'Run Same Command'
own brightness heuristic; light mode receives zero theming

verification.notes: Traced as written: LocalCmdConfirmationForm uses absolute pixel layout, never calls DialogTheme.SetDialogFont (every sibling script prompt — Confirm/Input/Choose/Multiselect — does), hard-codes the 140px "Run Same Command" button at lines 96-98, and gates all DialogTheme calls (incl. the Load-time ApplyNativeTheme) on its own GetBrightness()<0.2f copy of the private DialogTheme.ResolveDarkMode heuristic, leaving light mode fully unthemed; ScriptPromptDialogRunner applies nothing downstream. Two nits: ResolveDarkMode is currently private so the recommendation needs a visibility change, and the light-mode contrast is mainly the missing flat accent primary button/form colors (DialogTheme light-mode secondary buttons are also FlatStyle.Standard) rather than literally "raised 3D amid flat". Low severity is right.

title: Autocomplete popup is caged inside the editor control and collapses in short panes
existing_state: The completion popup is a Panel child of the UserControl, not a top-level window, so it can never extend past the editor's bounds: UpdateCompletionPopupSize clamps height to ClientSize.Height - 4 and width to ClientSize.Width - 4 (UI/ScintillaScriptEditorControl.cs:1242-1244), and CalculateCompletionPopupLocation clamps position into the client area (lines 1271-1273). With the splitter dragged down (or in JobEditorDialog where the custom-preset box shares a tab with the hosts grid), the 8-row list shrinks toward a single cramped row and long items lose their detail text, making completion near-useless exactly when screen space is scarce. Professional editors float the list over neighboring UI.
recommendation: Host the popup in a borderless ToolStripDropDown or a non-activating top-level Form (WS_EX_NOACTIVATE) positioned in screen coordinates from PointXFromPosition/PointYFromPosition, so it overlays the output pane/grid below the editor. The existing CompletionDismissMessageFilter and GetFocus-based dismissal logic (UI/ScintillaScriptEditorControl.cs:760-788) already handle out-of-hierarchy clicks, so most of the hard focus work is done.
user_benefit: Autocomplete stays fully usable regardless of how small the user has sized the script pane — no more one-row completion lists when the output pane is maximized during a debugging session.

evidence.note: Popup size clamped to the control's ClientSize
Popup location clamped inside the client area — cannot overlay neighbors

mockup_idea: Two panels: left, today — editor pane shrunk to ~5 visible lines, completion list squashed to one row clipped at the pane edge; right — same layout but the 8-row list floats over the output pane below the editor boundary.

verification.notes: Core claim verified: the popup is a Panel child of the UserControl (Controls.Add at ScintillaScriptEditorControl.cs:205), size is clamped to ClientSize-4 with a one-row floor (1242-1244), and position is clamped into the client area (1268-1273) — so dragging Form1's main splitter up does collapse the list toward one row, and detail text is dropped when width is tight (DrawItem, 1474-1503). However, the JobEditorDialog example is wrong: the custom-preset editor fills its own "Content" tab (JobEditorDialog.cs:439-460) and the hosts grid is on a separate "Hosts" tab, so they never share a tab and that scenario can't occur. The trigger is narrower than claimed (Form1 splitter only); severity low is still appropriate, and the recommendation's premise (existing dismiss filter/focus logic) checks out.

title: Default sample presets are unlabeled FortiGate CLI commands
existing_state: CreateDefaultConfiguration (Services/ConfigurationService.cs:427-440) seeds exactly two presets: 'Custom' → 'get system status' and 'Get external-address-resource list' → 'dia sys external-address-resource list'. Both are FortiGate-specific CLI, presented in the preset tree with no folder, no '(sample)' label, and no comment — a new user pointing the app at Linux or Cisco hosts who runs the pre-selected preset just gets command-not-found errors. The same two presets are also re-created after every corruption fallback (Load() returns CreateDefaultConfiguration at ConfigurationService.cs:99-101), so they can reappear and shadow a user's mental model.
recommendation: Replace the defaults with a 'Samples' folder containing vendor-neutral, clearly named entries — e.g. 'Sample: show system info' with a YAML script that uses send + a comment header explaining variables ({{Host_IP}}), and one tiny YAML sample demonstrating if/foreach so the scripting engine is discoverable. Prefix names with 'Sample:' or put them in a 'Samples' folder so they are visibly deletable boilerplate. ScriptSamples/ already has material to draw from.
user_benefit: First-run presets become a teaching aid instead of a vendor-specific trap; users on non-FortiGate fleets stop hitting confusing failures from the only two buttons the app gives them.

evidence.note: Hardcoded FortiGate commands as the only default presets, no sample labeling
Corruption fallback re-seeds the same presets
